Sad to see Balancer winding down:

I have fond memories using (and farming) it since day 1 but tbh I haven't used it for years now. So shutting down is understandable.

Interestingly, if the proposal passes, holders could redeem $BAL for their share of the treasury.

~$9.15M treasury vs ~$7.6M market cap.

Without treasury held $BAL and shutdown costs and we get ~11% upside at current prices. Still need to confirm how much BAL qualifies.

And unclaimed allocations go to those who redeem!

If 10% of eligible BAL goes unclaimed, the payout per redeemed token rises another ~11%.

So lost keys could benefit everyone else. I bet smart traders already calculating the trade.

But redemptions only start in May 2027, with unclaimed shares distributed by January 2028.

Quite a wait for that spread and lock in your capital...

Welcome to Fed Decision Day!
It is striking to see the market pricing in a 90% (yes 90%) probability of a rate hike today despite mixed economic data, uneven demand-side indicators, a delicate supply-side balance, a relatively dovish tone from several senior FOMC members, and a Chair intent on breaking the "hall of mirrors" phenomenon.
It is equally interesting to see how eagerly some market participants await the updated rate "dots," even as momentum builds against the current approach to forward guidance.
All this underscores just how difficult it is to evolve a Fed–market paradigm anchored by years of handholding, a constant stream of official commentary, excessive backward-looking data dependency, and a forward guidance regime that stumbled into spurious accuracy.
More to follow.
#economy #markets #federalreserve

There's currently a cambrian explosion of innovative onchain mechanisms

We're only just scratching the surface of how distributed systems can be used to leverage the "Wisdom of Crowds"

@umia_finance launched its UMIA token recently & will be incubating a number of high quality projects that'll be coming through its pipeline

But something I'm paying closer attention to the ongoing decision making & how these onchain mechanisms play into that process

Crypto made capital formation permissionless but left "control" of the capital largely unchanged

Teams sell tokens, take custody of the treasury, keep the IP inside a separate company & can treat token governance as advisory, with no consequences for ignoring outcomes

Tokenholders finance the business while remaining structurally downstream of it

Umia puts major project decisions through "conditional markets"; large treasury spend, acquisition, new issuance or strategic pivot creates two or more markets: 

i) one (or more) where the proposal passes, and; 
ii) a No-Op market where nothing changes

Traders price the project’s token under both futures & the proposal only executes if its TWAP beats the status quo by a defined threshold

This bit is super interesting to me because of the “Wisdom of Crowds” I mentioned above; it has somewhat been proven out in elections using prediction markets which have turned out to be more accurate than your average poll

Imagine a public company creating two temporary versions of its stock for every major board decision: 

i) one pricing the company if the deal happens, and; 
ii) one if it does not

The market that sustains the higher valuation determines what the company does...

Founders remain the C-suite, the market acts as the board, the treasury contract controls the money and the legal structure binds the development team to the outcome

This closes one of crypto’s largest structural gaps: linking tokenholder capital to enforceable control over how it’s used

The Clarity Act may have stalled yesterday, but pay attention to onchain mechanisms that enhance the ownership rights of tokenized businesses... it'll become increasingly important
